QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_66

question.text: In equity markets, what is the role of the 'Nifty Bank' index?

answer.text: It is a sectoral index comprising the most liquid and large-cap banking stocks, used as the underlying for banking sector index futures and options
It is the official interest rate index set by the RBI for banking sector
It is the list of banks authorized to clear derivative trades
It is the regulatory compliance score assigned to each bank by SEBI

explanation.text: The Logic: Nifty Bank (Bank Nifty) is a sectoral index composed of liquid, large-cap banking stocks listed on NSE. It serves as the underlying for Bank Nifty index futures and options, which are actively traded derivative contracts that allow participants to take views on or hedge exposure to the banking sector. The Trap: Bank Nifty is not an RBI interest-rate benchmark, not a list of clearing-eligible banks, and not a SEBI compliance score — it is a market-capitalisation-weighted stock index whose derivatives trade on NSE's F&O segment. Note: The Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages reviewed reference Bank Nifty as a non-benchmark index and as an underlying for futures/options expiry discussion, but do not explicitly state the sectoral-composition and liquidity claim. The framing above reflects general industry knowledge of NSE sectoral indices.
